Module 1 · 10 min

Labels that work

Why this matters: a field without a label is a guessing game for screen-reader users and a smaller click target for everyone else.

A <label> names a form control. Connect the two by giving the label a for attribute that matches the control's id:

<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" type="email">

A connected label is also clickable: pressing it focuses the control, so the effective target grows.

Common mistake: using placeholder as the label. It disappears as soon as someone starts typing.
Key takeaways
  • Every control needs a visible label.
  • The label's for must equal the control's id.
  • Clicking a connected label focuses its control.
